description: Edges lists every dependency edge of an explanation, as input and node pairs in the explanation's order
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
shipping = 5
subtotal = price * qty
total = subtotal + shipping
total |> why |> edges

description: Edges after affects lists the edges that a change travels, with the other inputs of the steps it reaches
code:
rate = 0.1
base = 100
fee = base * rate
total = base + fee
base |> affects |> edges

description: Edges over the model lists the edges of every node and leaves out the declarations that hold a stage
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
wiring = c |> why |> edges
model |> edges

description: A reference alone gives the edges into its own node
code:
width = 3
height = 4
area = width * height
area |> edges

description: Edges after stated is always empty, because a stated step has no inputs, and after derived it lists every edge
code:
x = 2
y = x * 3
[y |> why |> stated |> edges, y |> why |> derived |> edges]

description: Edges keeps the edges from inputs that a depth-limited selection leaves out
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b + 1
d = c + 1
why d |> depth(1) |> edges

description: Edges after union lists the edges of both explanations, each node once
code:
a = 1
b = a + 2
c = 5
d = c + a
b |> why |> union(d |> why) |> edges

description: A standing declaration that holds edges follows a rewiring: the new input's edge appears and the dropped one goes
code:
a = 1
x = 5
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
wiring = c |> why |> edges
b = x * 2
wiring

description: A change of a value alone leaves the edges as they are
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
wiring = b |> why |> edges
a = 7
wiring

description: A class-level rule that holds edges gives each instance the edges of its own property
code:
rate = 2
class Part(cost):
    this.cost = cost
$Part.price = $Part.cost * rate
$Part.links = $Part.price |> why |> edges
bolt = Part(3)
bolt.links

description: Mapping each edge to an arrow renders an explanation as a graph
code:
hours = 8
pay = 20
wage = hours * pay
bonus = 50
total = wage + bonus
(total |> why |> edges).map(edge -> edge.join(" -> "))

description: Filtering edges by the names that nodes gives keeps only the edges between the steps of a selection
code:
price = 10
qty = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * qty
tax = subtotal * rate
total = subtotal + tax
kept = total |> why |> except(subtotal) |> nodes
(total |> why |> except(subtotal) |> edges).filter(edge -> kept.includes(edge[0]))
